title: Dynamics & tempo terms
examples: What is the difference between forte and piano?
Can you show me how to read a tempo marking?
What does allegro mean in music?

explain.say: Today we are learning some Italian words for music.
Next we will look at dynamic markings in music.
A tempo marking tells you the speed of the music.
We can also use symbols to show changes in volume.
In real life, you use these ideas when performing music.
A common mistake is confusing the Italian words.

faq.q: What does crescendo mean in music?
faq.a: Crescendo means a gradual increase in the loudness of the sound. It shows the music getting louder over time.
asks: How do I make music louder gradually?

faq.q: What is the difference between tempo and dynamics?
faq.a: Tempo refers to the speed of the music, like fast or slow. Dynamics refer to the volume, like loud or soft.
asks: Is tempo about speed or volume?
What changes do tempo and dynamics control?

faq.q: Are there other Italian tempo terms?
faq.a: Yes, there are many. Andante means at a walking pace, and Moderato means moderately or at a medium speed.
asks: Do I need to know all the Italian terms?

faq.q: What do the symbols p and f mean?
faq.a: P stands for piano, which means soft. F stands for forte, which means loud. They are basic volume markings.
asks: How do I know if I should play loudly or softly?

faq.q: Can I use these terms in non-musical contexts?
faq.a: The concepts can be used in other areas. For example, describing how a voice builds up in intensity.
asks: Is this only for music class?
Can I use this idea for speaking?

facts: Allegro is an Italian term meaning fast and lively.
Piano (p) indicates a soft volume, while forte (f) indicates a loud volume.
Crescendo is a gradual increase in sound intensity.
Tempo markings describe the speed or pace of the music.

quiz.say: If a piece of music starts softly and gets louder, which dynamic marking is being used?
quiz.why: Crescendo specifically means the sound is getting louder over time.

wrong.0: Piano only tells you the sound should be soft, not that it is getting louder.
wrong.1: Forte only tells you the sound should be loud, not that it is changing.
wrong.2: Allegro describes the speed, not the change in volume.

quiz.say: Which Italian term suggests a very slow and graceful tempo?
quiz.why: Adagio is the specific Italian term used for a slow and graceful pace.

wrong.0: Presto means very fast, which is much quicker than slow.
wrong.1: Andante means a walking pace, which is usually faster than adagio.
wrong.3: Allegro means fast and lively, which is the opposite of slow.

quiz.say: If a piece of music is marked 'p' at the start and then gets softer, what is the sequence of dynamics?
quiz.why: The music starts soft (p) and then gets softer, which is the definition of diminuendo.

wrong.0: Crescendo means getting louder, so this sequence is incorrect.
wrong.1: Allegro is a tempo term, not a dynamic change.
wrong.3: This would mean going from soft to loud, which is the opposite of what is described.
